plain: To coax someone with flattery or false promises.

webster.text: To flatter; to soothe; to coax; to deceive or delude by flattery.

example.quote: At some time, it has been said that 1 have not been at the pains to conceal my contempt of the people ; but when it suits a purpose better, it is asserted that I cajole them.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Pennsylvania Convention, Mr. WILSON, December 4, 1787 (2d ed. 1836)
